title: Israel Police disable internal systems over fear of leaking sensitive information; cause unconfirmed
date_note: Arab48 relays a Ynet report of Monday 23 November; the page gives no earlier day than the day of the report, though it says the technical incident began on Sunday.
summary: Arab48, relaying Ynet, reports that Israel Police disabled several internal systems and applications out of fear that sensitive and classified information could leak, after a technical incident that began on Sunday. The article says it is not yet known whether this was a cyberattack or an external technical fault. According to the report, police personnel will be asked to update their passwords.
plain: Arab48, citing Ynet, says Israeli police switched off internal systems for fear of a leak. It is not known whether it was an attack or a fault. Officers must change passwords.
exec: A national police force took internal systems offline as a precaution, according to Arab48 relaying Ynet; the cause is not confirmed.
geo_basis: national police force; the article names no city (point placed at Jerusalem)

validation.note: Only Arab48 was read (via a fetch sub-agent), relaying Ynet; the original Ynet report and any police statement were not read.

review.note: title, summary, Sunday start, unknown cause, password update checked against Arab48 (23 Nov), which attributes to Ynet; single_source, developing correct
